'''Raymond "RayJ" Patterson Dennis''' (born March 30, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Atlanta Hawks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[College Park Skyhawks]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Boise State Broncos men's basketball|Boise State Broncos]], the [[Toledo Rockets men's basketball|Toledo Rockets]] and the [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor Bears]].

==High school career==
Before high school, Dennis attended Heritage Grove Middle School and Murphy Jr. High in Plainfield, Illinois. Dennis attended [[Montini Catholic High School]] for two seasons. For his junior year, he transferred to [[Oswego East High School]] and averaged 17.2 points and 4.9 assists per game.<ref name="glorfield">{{cite news |last=Glorfield |first=Chase |date=September 10, 2018 |title=RayJ Dennis Gives Boise State Their Guard Of the Future |url=https://247sports.com/college/boise-state/Article/RayJ-Dennis-Gives-Boise-State-Their-Guard-Of-the-Future-121703360/ |access-date=June 9, 2023 |work=[[247Sports]]}}</ref> As a senior, he averaged 23.2 points, 5.1 assists, 4.9 rebounds and 2.5 steals per game.<ref name="hughes">{{cite news |last=Hughes |first=Grant |date=June 1, 2023 |title=RayJ Dennis commits to Baylor basketball: Toledo transfer PG, portal's No. 31 player, chooses Bears |url=https://247sports.com/article/rayj-dennis-commits-to-baylor-basketball-toledo-transfer-pg-port-210682955/ |access-date=June 9, 2023 |work=247 Sports}}</ref> Dennis committed to play college basketball at [[Boise State Broncos men's basketball|Boise State]], choosing the Broncos over 26 [[NCAA Division I|Division I]] offers.<ref name="glorfield"/>

==College career==
As a freshman, Dennis averaged 4.1 points, 1.8 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game. He posted 8.6 points, 3.0 rebounds and a team-best 2.9 assists per game as a sophomore. Dennis opted to transfer to [[Toledo Rockets men's basketball|Toledo]] after the season.<ref>{{cite web |date=April 13, 2021 |title=RayJ Dennis Joining Rockets' Program |url=https://utrockets.com/news/2021/4/13/mens-basketball-rayj-dennis-joining-rockets-program.aspx |access-date=June 9, 2023 |work=[[Toledo Rockets]]}}</ref> Dennis averaged 12.7 points, 4.0 assists and 5.6 rebounds per game as a junior.<ref name="hughes"/> On March 3, 2023, he scored a career-high 32 points to go with seven assists in a 87–81 win over [[2022–23 Ball State Cardinals men's basketball team|Ball State]].<ref>{{cite news |date=March 3, 2023 |title=Dennis scores 32, Toledo defeats Ball State 87-81 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401473608 |access-date=June 9, 2023 |work=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> As a senior, Dennis averaged 19.5 points, 4.3 rebounds and 5.8 assists per game, leading Toledo to a 27–8 record and [[Mid-American Conference]] (MAC) regular-season championship. He was named [[Mid-American Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|MAC Player of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web | title=RayJ Dennis Earns MAC Player of Year Honors | website=University of Toledo Athletics | date=March 8, 2023| url=https://utrockets.com/news/2023/3/7/mens-basketball-rayj-dennis-earns-mac-player-of-year-honors | access-date=2025-12-05}}</ref> Following the season he transferred to [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]], choosing the Bears over [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]], [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] and [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=June 1, 2023 |title=Baylor lands Toledo guard RayJ Dennis out of transfer portal |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/37774230 |access-date=June 9, 2023 |work=[[ESPN]]}}</ref>

==Professional career==
After going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Dennis joined the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] for the [[2024 NBA Summer League]]<ref>{{cite web |title=2024 NBA2K25 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2024/las-vegas/team/1610612746/clippers |access-date=September 14, 2024 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> and on September 6, 2024, he signed with the team.<ref>{{cite web |last=Adams |first=Luke |date=September 6, 2024 |title=Clippers Sign RayJ Dennis To Exhibit 10 Deal |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/09/clippers-rayj-dennis-agree-to-exhibit-10-deal.html |access-date=September 6, 2024 |website=HoopsRumors.com}}</ref> However, on October 9, he was waived.<ref>{{cite web |last=Adams |first=Luke |date=October 9, 2024 |title=Clippers Waive RayJ Dennis, Re-Sign Elijah Harkless |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/clippers-waive-rayj-dennis.html |access-date=October 9, 2024 |website=HoopsRumors.com}}</ref> On October 19, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Washington Wizards]],<ref>{{cite web |date=October 19, 2024 |title=Wizards Sign RayJ Dennis To Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-sign-rayj-dennis-to-two-way-contract |access-date=October 21, 2024 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> but was waived two days later.<ref>{{cite web |date=October 21, 2024 |title=Wizards Announce 2024-25 Opening Night Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-announce-2024-25-opening-night-roster |access-date=October 21, 2024 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On October 28, he joined the [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web |date=October 28, 2024 |title=SAN DIEGO CLIPPERS ANNOUNCE TRAINING CAMP ROSTER FOR 2024-25 NBA G LEAGUE SEASON |url=https://sandiego.gleague.nba.com/news/san-diego-clippers-announce-training-camp-roster-for-2024-25-nba-g-league-season |access-date=November 2, 2024 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

On January 3, 2025, Dennis signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web |date=January 3, 2025 |title=Indiana Pacers Sign RayJ Dennis to a Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/indiana-pacers-sign-rayj-dennis-to-a-two-way-contract |access-date=January 3, 2025 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He made 11 appearances for the Pacers during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 2.7 points, 1.1 rebounds and 1.3 assists.

Dennis played in 13 games for Indiana during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], posting averages of 4.9 points, 1.6 rebounds and 2.0 assists. Dennis was waived by the Pacers on November 30, 2025, following the signing of [[Ethan Thompson]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Indiana Pacers Sign Ethan Thompson to a Two-Way Contract |url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/the-indiana-pacers-sign-ethan-thompson-to-a-two-way-contract |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=The NBA G League |language=en}}</ref>

On December 5, 2025, Dennis signed a two-way contract with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-12-05 |title=RayJ Dennis Returns to Clippers Organization, Signs Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/rayj-dennis-returns-to-clippers-organization-signs-two-way-contract/n-6306226 |url-status=live |access-date=2025-12-06 |publisher=OurSports Central |language=en}}</ref> He made one appearance for Los Angeles, going scoreless in four minutes during a 122–101 loss to the [[2025–26 Oklahoma City Thunder season|Oklahoma City Thunder]] on December 18. On December 29, Dennis was waived by the Clippers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NBA Fantasy Basketball News (December 2025) {{!}} RotoWire |url=https://www.rotowire.com/basketball/news.php |access-date=2025-12-31 |website=rotowire.com}}</ref>

On December 31, 2025, Dennis signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Guard RayJ Dennis to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-guard-rayj-dennis-to-two-way-contract-2 |access-date=2026-07-24 |website=NBA.com |language=en|date=2025-12-31}}</ref> On January 16, 2026, while playing for the [[College Park Skyhawks]], Dennis recorded 46 points and 15 assists in a 140–155 loss to the [[Delaware Blue Coats]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Two-Way RayJ Dennis Erupted for 46 PTS & 15 AST vs. the Blue Coats|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/two-way-rayj-dennis-erupted-for-46-pts--15-ast-vs-the-blue-coats/n-6317837|access-date=February 2, 2026|website=oursportscentral.com|language=en|date=January 16, 2026}}</ref>
